title: Latency Budgets: Tails, Streaming, Parallelism
objective: After this lesson you will be able to budget p50/p95/p99 across agent stages, parallelize independent calls, stream partials to hide latency, and bound every call with timeouts that protect the tail.
why: Users feel p99, averages lie: a 1.2s median with 12s tails reads as 'slow and flaky'. Agent latency stacks serially (4 model calls × tails), retrieval outliers add, tool timeouts hang. Budgeting allocates milliseconds per stage like money, then spends parallelism, streaming, and timeouts to fit — measured per tier, never assumed.

blocks.text: Four serial 300ms-median calls with occasional 3s tails yield p99 ≈ sum of tails, not medians: serial chains **add tail risk**. Measure per-stage p50/p95/p99 separately (model, retrieval, tools) before optimizing — the budget table shows which stage owns the tail, and only that stage deserves surgery.

blocks.caption: Percentile budgets per stage: tails allocated like money

blocks.text: Independent calls (policy fetch + order lookup + history) run **concurrently**: tail becomes max-of-tails, not sum. Promise.all with per-call timeouts (slowest bounded, not waited on forever); dependent calls stay serial by necessity. Dependency analysis (which inputs need which outputs?) precedes every parallelization — parallelizing dependent calls corrupts, not accelerates.

blocks.caption: Concurrent independents, bounded each, serial only by necessity

blocks.text: **Streaming** (token-by-token delivery) converts waiting into reading: perceived latency drops to time-to-first-token even when totals hold. **Timeouts** bound every call with fallback routing on breach (Ch.4 cascades): a 1.5s retrieval timeout failing over beats a 12s hang succeeding. Perceived + bounded beats merely fast on average.

blocks.title: Find the tail owner
blocks.note: Run it: retrieval owns ~60% and breaches allowance — the only stage earning surgery. Triage and draft stay untouched: budgets direct effort, not hunches.

items: Budget p50/p95/p99 per stage; serial tails add — tail owner gets surgery, others don't
Parallelize independents (max-of-tails) with per-call timeouts; dependents stay serial
Stream to hide (time-to-first-token), timeout to bound (breach routes to fallbacks)

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice budget and name the tail owner with shares. (b) Parallelize retrieval+draft hypothetically (are they independent? check inputs) and recompute serial p99 honestly. (c) Set a timeout for retrieval with fallback routing and state what users see on breach.
hints: Owner: retrieval ~60% + OVER. Others within allowance — untouched by discipline.
Dependency check: draft needs retrieval output → dependent, stays serial. Only truly independent calls parallelize (policy fetch + order lookup pattern).
Timeout 2000ms → fallback (cached/stale-labeled or simplified answer): breach shows degraded-but-fast, never hangs.
exercise.why: Dependency analysis before parallelization plus timeout-with-fallback design are the two latency judgments: speedups must preserve correctness, bounds must preserve experience.
exercise.code: // Budget-then-parallelize pattern: measure shares, check dependencies, bound tails.

quiz.q: p50 1.2s, p99 12s, 4 serial model calls. Biggest lever?
options: Parallelize independents + stream + timeout tails: serial chains add tail risk; tails dominate p99
quiz.explain: p99 is tail arithmetic: serial sums, parallel takes max, streaming hides, timeouts bound. Measure per stage first.

options: No: dependents stay serial — parallelizing corrupts inputs; parallelize independents only
quiz.explain: Dependency analysis gates parallelism: independent calls concurrent, dependent calls serial. Speed never overrides correctness.

options: Labeled fallback (cached/stale-marked or simplified) — bounded degraded beats unbounded perfect
quiz.explain: Timeouts route to fallbacks (Ch.4): fast-degraded with honesty labels preserves trust that hangs destroy.

summary: Percentile budgets per stage, parallelism for independents, streaming for perception, timeouts for bounds. Tails measured, owned, and operated.
